ImageDescription.value: These microscopic butterflies are surely one of the smallest, lightest and likely most expensive ones in the world as they partially consist of the novel one atom thick material graphene. Such butterflies however are not synthesized for their beauty, but in order to get valuable information about the electrochemical properties of graphene! By using a high resolution scanning electron microscope (SEM) to study how polypyrrole had electrochemically deposited on graphene islands, it was possible to visualize how active the defects in graphene really are compared to the defect free areas. Using the gained knowledge it was possible to synthesize an ultra thin graphene-polypyrrole nanocomposite corrosion resistant coating. This study is published in Synthetic Metals and the development of the coating can also be seen in our science video in Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D3CVN48B_zQ

Artist.value: Maido Merisalu

ImageDescription.value: Image of the birch veneer’s surface with a hole shot with a 40W CO2 laser using scanning electron microscope Helons Nanolab 600 (FEI Company). While the hole appeared black to the naked eye, scanning electron microscopy can visualize the microstructure at the edges of the hole. For imaging, the veneer was pre-coated with a thin layer of platinum to prevent the surface from getting charged by the accelerated electrons. In the film technology laboratory of the Institute of Physics of the University of Tartu, various techniques are often used to study the interior of materials, which sometimes requires the production of a high-quality cut cross-sections. For smaller nanostructures, a focused ion beam is used for this purpose, but in this case it was more practical to use a CO2 laser.

Artist.value: Kent Gregor Mahla, Maido Merisalu

ImageDescription.value: “Nanocigarette”. Upon heating silica coated silver nanowires (diameter ~ 100 nm) to 600 °C silver (brighter material on the images) starts to swell out of the silica shell and by doing so, starts to break the shell and accumulate at the end of the wire (creating a “cloud of smoke”). Thickness of the silica shell is only about 30 nm, so it is almost transparent for electrons and therefore it can be seen that some of the silver is still encapsulated the shell. Image is taken in the Institute of Physics, University of Tartu using a scanning electron microscope (FEI Nova NanoSEM 450). Author: Mikk Vahtrus.

ImageDescription.value: A bridge was formed during electrochemical synthesis. The electric field is the strongest on the tip - somehow two tips formed opposite each other from the general polymer surface and grew together. This could be a new method for fiber synthesis. In science everything does not usually succeed in the first try. For every success story there are hundreds if not thousands of tries gone wrong. But once in a while an anomaly could be the source of a major breakthrough. Here is a compilation of anomalies that impress with interesting shapes and have inspired new methods. This scanning electron microscopy image was taken at the Institute of Technology University of Tartu during the research work of polypyrrole actuators.

Artist.value: Kadri-Ann Valdur, Tarmo Tamm, Indrek Must

ImageDescription.value: The electrochemical synthesis of polypyrrole involves applying current to electrodes in a solution containing the monomer pyrrole. This scanning electron microscopy image was taken at the Institute of Technology University of Tartu during the research work of polypyrrole actuators.

ImageDescription.value: Image of a wood veneer surface taken with a scanning electron microscope using secondary electrons. To take the picture, the wood had to be first covered with a thin film of platinum, which made it electrically conductive. Helios Nanolab 600 (FEI Company) scanning electron microscope of the Film Technology Laboratory of the Institute of Physics of the University of Tartu was then used to visualize the invisible to the human eye microstructure of wood.

ImageDescription.value: A thin film of polypyrrole formed on a stainless steel electrode. The electrochemical synthesis of polypyrrole involves applying current to electrodes in a solution containing the monomer pyrrole. It is considered an effective and precise method for thin film manufacturing. Here is a compilation of polypyrrole thin films. This scanning electron microscopy image was taken at the Institute of Technology University of Tartu during the research work of polypyrrole actuators.

ImageDescription.value: This material makes trains float in the air. Supersmall picture of a superconductor. At relatively low temperatures (95 K, -178.15 <sup>0</sup>C) this superconductor material Yttrium barium copper oxide, which crystals are seen on the picture could be compared to Napoleon. Instead of leading soldiers to war, this material leads electrons where needed without any significant resistance.  Even though the  YBa<sub>2</sub>Cu<sub>3</sub>O<sub>7</sub><sub>−x</sub>  crystals are small their influence in macroscopic levels is significant.  They are used in superconducing supermagnets and technologies of high-speed trains (ca 600 km/h).
